threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the tube' instead of just 'overground' when you're catching a train from Clapton. It's a dead giveaway.
Last night on the 333, I saw a guy trying to sell homemade candles to a woman who just wanted to get home. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy casually walking his pet iguana on a leash by the canal, I knew I was in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can casually hop off a bus mid-route in Kreuzberg and enjoy an impromptu street concert. The spontaneous vibe is a Berlin hallmark!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they can name the taco truck with the longest line on a Tuesday. Tourists don’t get the allure.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where the driver tried to calm a guy yelling about pigeons stealing his snacks. Classic S.F. chaos on a Tuesday.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all we do is party in Gràcia, but half the night is spent listening to our neighbours argue over their pets' names.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their bewilderment at the '1.5-hour' wait for tapas on a Saturday night—like they’re waiting for a flight instead of dinner.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wince when you see the Dalston Junction on a Google map, but locals just shrug and hop on the Overground like it’s a corner shop.
Last night on the 36, saw a guy trying to impress a girl by singing the entire '90s theme from Fresh Prince. She just rolled her eyes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw an old man arguing with a pigeon over bread crumbs outside the Spätkauf. Classic Neukölln moments.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you see a spontaneous dance party break out in the U-Bahn station at 3 AM after a night out. It's like the city's heartbeat.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by their ability to navigate the BART delays without breaking a sweat, while newcomers are still staring at their screens in confusion.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy offering to trade his burrito for a Muni transfer. Only in San Francisco would food and transit go hand in hand like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the boquerias are the same. Try the one on Gran de Gràcia for local vibes, no lines, and the best olives you've ever tasted.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they ask for tapas – if they pronounce 'patatas bravas' like a tourist, they're fresh off the plane.
